    Fill-In by Greedy Selection with Candidate Sufficiency Checks

    fill_in.Rd

    At each iteration: 1. Builds a fixed pool of candidate points (interior lattice + uniform boundary), truncated to the original box. 2. Checks that the candidate pool size is at least max_add. 3. Greedily selects the candidate farthest from the current design, appends it, and recomputes fill_in. 4. Stops when fill_in <= h or max_add points have been added.

    fill_in(
  boss_result,
  h,
  max_add = 100,
  grid_n = 200,
  boundary_n = 200,
  verbose = 0
)

    Arguments

    boss_result

    A boss object with non-NULL essential_support and essential_design_points\$x_original, and containing lower and upper.

    h

    Numeric; target fill-in distance (>= 0).

    max_add

    Integer; maximum number of points to add (default 100).

    grid_n

    Integer; resolution per axis for interior lattice (default 200).

    boundary_n

    Integer; number of boundary samples (default 200).

    verbose

    Integer in {0,1,2,3}; 0=silent, 1=summary, (>=)2=per-iteration.

    Value

    The updated boss_result, with its essential_design_points and fill_in refreshed.

    Details

    If the candidate pool is too small to potentially reach max_add, or if even the best candidate cannot reduce fill_in below h, a warning is issued.
